title: refresh-auth-deps and fix token-parsing edge cases
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Replace and pin several aging authentication and crypto dependencies across the runtime and control plane to remediate recent CVE reports, close parsing edge-cases in token handling, and minimize behavioral changes for customers. This ticket covers: OpenSSL/libssl upgrades in base images, migrating JWT libraries to maintained forks, and applying hardening fixes to SAML/SSO libraries used by the private control plane. The goal is low-risk rollouts with canary traffic, improved unit/fuzz coverage for token parsing, and updated build pipelines to verify pinned checksums.
acceptance_criteria: All listed CVEs addressed or documented with compensating controls
OpenSSL upgraded to agreed target version and base images rebuilt with pinned checksums
JWT parsing moved to golang-jwt v4 (or equivalent) with backward-compatible behavior for our token formats
SAML/SSO library patches applied and tested for large assertion payloads and invalid-attribute cases
Unit, integration, and new fuzz tests added and passing in CI
Canary rollout performed to Dedicated infra and monitored for three days with no auth regressions
KMS/HSM integrations unaffected and E2E internal SSO flows pass
steps: Inventory all services that import or vendor OpenSSL/JWT/SAML libraries and produce a dependency matrix
Select target stable upstream versions and capture commits/pinned SHAs to vendor and CI manifests
Implement code adapters where APIs changed (e.g., new claims parsing interfaces) to preserve existing behavior
Add fuzz tests specifically for token parsing (long sub/jti, unexpected control chars, null bytes)
Rebuild base images, run full regression suite, and publish artifacts to internal registry
Create GitHub PRs per repo with CHANGELOG and migration notes; request security and runtime reviews
Deploy canaries to Dedicated nodepool and monitor auth metrics and error rates for 72 hours
Roll out to Hosted API with feature flag and staged traffic increase if canary stable
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope and target versions (OpenSSL 3.1.2, golang-jwt v4.0.0), owners assigned.
2025-02-18: Completed dependency inventory across 14 repos; created mapping in Confluence (https://confluence.company.com/display/PLAT/Auth+Dep+Inventory).
2025-02-24: Prototype adapter for JWT claim de-serialisation in runtime repo; discovered subtle difference in time validation semantics requiring a compatibility shim.
2025-02-28: Raised PR runtime#8123 to vendor golang-jwt v4 and add compatibility shim; tests failing in legacy token fixtures — investigating.
2025-03-02: Security review scheduled; draft threat model added (https://confluence.company.com/display/SEC/JWT+parsing+threats).
2025-03-05: Fuzz harness for token parser merged, found three edge-cases (null bytes, malformed base64 padding, oversized kid header) — fixes in progress.
notes: Trade-offs: Full API surface behavioral parity is higher-risk and increases patch volume. We will use compatibility shims where possible and document any minor behavior changes.
If a library upgrade requires changes that materially affect latency (e.g., different crypto provider fallback), we will gate that change behind a runtime config and evaluate against cost SLOs.
Coordinate with SE and Support teams before Hosted rollout; prepare rollback plan referencing image digest to revert quickly.
